accuracy_evidence: Retained rankings and run.json evidence support advancement and final accuracy. Wide configured advance=5 and its top five were luna-medium, gpt55-low, gpt55-medium, spark-medium, terra-low; semifinal run candidates matched exactly. Semifinal configured advance=3 and its top three were luna-medium, terra-low, gpt55-low; final run candidates matched exactly. In final, all three candidates had accuracy=1.0, verdict_accuracy=1.0, precision=1.0, recall=1.0, and f1=1.0 across the three final fixtures.
cost_evidence: Final ranking correctly used estimated Codex credit cost after the equal accuracy tier: luna-medium 1.6152 credits, terra-low 4.3022375 credits, gpt55-low 8.8513 credits. These are not within the 15 percent equivalence band of the cheaper candidate, so the cost order supports luna-medium first.
speed_evidence: Wall time was only tertiary. Final wall times were luna-medium 28.77944487379864s, terra-low 23.93769308226183s, and gpt55-low 27.97033612523228s. Terra-low was faster than luna-medium, but speed did not override the non-equivalent cost difference under the configured policy.
limitations: The evaluation covers only five seeded fixtures: one wide, one semifinal, and three final fixtures.
Seeded-fixture performance demonstrates behavior against known artificial cases, not complete real-page conformance review coverage.
The review accepts the retained tournament evidence as supplied and does not rescore from intuition or inspect model responses outside the requested run.json artifacts.
Unpriced candidates existed in earlier stages, but the final ranking only contains priced candidates, so the accepted winner is not provisional for missing price data.
recommendation: Accept luna-medium as the supported tournament winner for the retained evaluation artifacts.
